notes: Small Wisconsin-only chain/franchise system (about 22-24 locations in 2025 per Urban Milwaukee/ESPN; Wikipedia says 31), so chain=false per task instructions. ORIGINAL location (opened May 1948 at E Ogden Ave & N Van Buren St, Milwaukee) is no longer a George Webb; when it closed was not found. name: Pizza Man

name: National Bakery & Deli

name: Wisconsin Cheese Mart

Overture also lists 1220 E Meinecke Ave (status blank; possibly a warehouse - unverified). No hours found on site; price_tier null (retail store). Appeared in Google's Gemini ad during Super Bowl LIX (Feb 2025); moved to notes since it is an ad appearance, not an honor.

name: Usinger's Famous Sausage

Mimi Sheraton praise (1973) is a quote, not an honor. price_tier null (retail meat market).

name: American Serb Hall
iconic_reason: Banquet hall built in 1950 and run by St. Sava Serbian Orthodox Cathedral that has served a Friday fish fry since 1967, now with dine-in, drive-thru and walk-up service.
open_evidence: https://cbs58.com/news/every-friday-i-come-here-fish-frys-fill-up-for-first-friday-of-lent - CBS58 (Mar 7, 2025) reports American Serb Hall serving its Lenten Friday fish fry, quoting board president Sonja Vujatovic; official food-services page (seen Sep 2026) lists Friday fish fry 3:30-8:30pm dine-in, drive-thru and walk-up.
notes: The brief said Serb Hall was sold around 2020 and renamed; that is NOT what sources show. No rename found: the formal name is American Serb Memorial Hall, commonly American Serb Hall / Serb Hall. Fish fry went carry-out/drive-thru only 2020-2022 and dine-in resumed Feb 17, 2023. 'founded' 1950 = year the hall was built per Urban Milwaukee; the official site says 'over 75 years' (consistent); the fish fry itself began in 1967. The hall also has a bowling center at the same address. Official site claims 'Voted Milwaukee's favorite fish fry 5 years in a row' (no granting body named, so not listed as an honor). Price tier not determined (no current priced menu fetched). Long-time stop for presidential and political visits (Milwaukee Magazine).

name: The Packing House

Drive-thru fish fry (cash only, Fridays 3-9pm) reportedly dates to the late 1980s (search snippet only, not verified). Building previously housed Dutch's Sukiyaki House. Price tier 2 based on fish fry $21.95-27.95; steak prices not checked. Official site shows a 2023 Mayor's Design Award image for its patio (not independently verified, so not listed as an honor). NPR (Oct 2024) described it as a classic Wisconsin supper club. Kept here (not on the supper-club list) because its own site describes it as a family-owned scratch-kitchen restaurant, not a supper club; the 'supper club' tag was removed.

name: Lakefront Brewery
iconic_reason: Craft brewery founded by brothers Russ and Jim Klisch in 1987 whose riverside beer hall hosts a Friday fish fry with a live polka band.
open_evidence: https://wtmj.com/news/2026/01/14/lakefront-brewery-owner-plans-new-outdoor-amenities/ - WTMJ (Jan 14, 2026) on owner Russ Klisch's plans for new outdoor amenities; official beer hall page (seen Sep 2026) lists daily hours and Friday fish fry from 4pm with the Brewhaus Polka Kings 5-8pm.

Also has a warehouse at 3519 N Hubbard St (Overture) and acquired Kenosha's Public Craft Brewing (Urban Milwaukee press release, date not checked). Per Wikipedia (not independently re-verified): first U.S. brewery to bottle a fruit beer after Prohibition (Cherry Lager, 1992), nation's first certified organic brewery (1996), and petitioned the federal TTB to approve New Grist, described as the first gluten-free beer in America (year not given); these are 'firsts', not granted honors, so other_honors is left empty. Russ Klisch was reported as a 2025 Entrepreneur of the Year award winner (granting body not identified, not listed). Wikipedia also says TripAdvisor named it #4 brewery tour in America (2010) - not listed. WISN reported tariff losses of $400-500k equaling about 4% of revenue (implies roughly $10-12M, but no revenue figure is directly reported, so left null). Price tier not determined (menu PDFs not read).

name: Wolski's Tavern
iconic_reason: Lower East Side corner tavern opened in 1908 by Bernard Wolski, still run by his great-grandsons, known for its 'I Closed Wolski's' bumper stickers handed out since 1973.
open_evidence: https://punchdrink.com/articles/i-closed-wolskis-tavern-milwaukee-bar/ - PUNCH feature (Feb 19, 2025) on the operating bar with owner Bernie Bondar and staff; official site (seen Sep 2026) lists current hours daily 2pm/noon to 2-2:30am.

Owners: brothers Bernie and Dennis Bondar (great-grandsons), who took over in 1973. TMJ4 published an undated farewell to longtime bartender Mike Bondar (credited with the stickers) saying the tavern will remain open - date of his death not determined. Food: essentially none (free popcorn; food trucks at events), so food relevance is low. Wikipedia notes Esquire's 2012 naming of Milwaukee 'Best Bar City' featured the bar - not listed as a specific honor for the bar.

other_honors: Tales of the Cocktail Foundation Timeless U.S. Award (2026)

open_evidence: https://www.wisn.com/article/milwaukees-bryants-cocktail-lounge-earns-prestigious-global-recognition/71844674 - WISN (Jul 7, 2026) reports Bryant's received the 2026 Timeless Award from the Tales of the Cocktail Foundation; official site (seen Sep 2026) lists hours Tue-Sun.
notes: Founding year: official homepage says 'Open since 1938' and WISN says it first opened in 1938, but the official history page says it opened as a beer hall in August 1936 and became a cocktail lounge circa 1938; used 1938 (the business's headline claim). Pink Squirrel invention claim is the bar's own (also on Wikipedia's Pink Squirrel page) - not an independent verification. Urban Milwaukee's 2017 Bar Exam headline also says 'Serving Cocktails Since 1936'. Ownership: Bryant Sharp (d. early 1960s), then Pat Malmberg; John Dye has owned it since 2008 (Urban Milwaukee, Jul 7, 2026); site copyright is Buckaroo LTD, and Dye's group also runs At Random and (since 2025) Von Trier. Rebuilt after a St. Patrick's Day 1971 fire. No food; cocktails only, so food relevance is low.

name: Von Trier
iconic_reason: German-style East Side bar at North and Farwell avenues since July 1978, on a corner that housed Rieder's Cocktail Lounge from 1949, which added a full German kitchen in 2018.
open_evidence: https://www.vontriers.com/christmas-tour-2026 - official site (seen Sep 2026) lists current hours with kitchen until 10pm and promotes a 'Von Trier European Christmas Tour' for Nov 30 - Dec 9, 2026.
notes: Ownership changes per the bar's own history page: Karl Lotharius opened Von Trier in July 1978 (predecessor Rieder's Cocktail Lounge, Frank Rieder, 1949-1978); Lotharius was murdered in 1981 (unsolved) and Mark Eckert ran/owned it 1981-2009; John and Cindy Sidoff owned it 2009-2025; John Dye (Bryant's/At Random group) acquired it in 2025. Independent support is partial: Urban Milwaukee (Mar 13, 2025, paywalled) ran 'Historic Bar Getting New Operator' with the subhead 'Seasoned proprietor John Dye will expand his collection of historic taverns' - the bar's name was behind the paywall, so whether it was a purchase or an operating/lease deal is not confirmed. Kitchen added 2018. No independent 2025-2026 news article found; open status rests on the official site.

name: Koz's Mini Bowl
iconic_reason: South Side corner tavern with four short duckpin-style bowling lanes installed in 1947 and hand-set pins, run by the Kosakoski family as Koz's since 1978.
open_evidence: https://www.milwaukeemag.com/the-best-things-to-do-this-week-according-to-our-editors-jan-5/ - Milwaukee Magazine things-to-do list (Jan 2026) recommends Koz's as a duckpin bowling dive bar 'since 1947'; CBS58 feature Jan 16, 2024; Overture Sep-2026 extract lists 'Historic Koz's Mini Bowl' as open.
notes: Founding: DuWayne Roger Kosakoski opened it as Koz's Mini Bowl in May 1978 (Urban Milwaukee 2016); the building dates to 1890 (saloon, dining room, dance hall) and the mini lanes were installed in 1947 under original operator Bosko Kresovich; Mike Lakic ran it as Mike's Park View Bowl 1971-1978. Milwaukee Magazine dates it 'since 1947' (the lanes). Used 1978 for the Koz's business; 1947 would be defensible for the lane tavern. Listed for sale Aug 2022 at $499,000, delisted Dec 2022; owner son Justin Kosakowski (spelled Kosakowski in 2022 article vs Kosakoski in 2016) said he planned to keep running it. Lanes are 4 short lanes (Urban Milwaukee 2022 says 17-foot duckpin lanes). Address is 7th St near Lincoln Ave (Urban Milwaukee calls it Historic Mitchell Street neighborhood, not Bay View). No food menu found; food relevance low. Official site kozsminibowl.com could not be loaded (SSL error), so no official hours checked. Jan 2026 evidence is a listing/recommendation, not a visit report.

name: Holler House
iconic_reason: South Side tavern opened by the Skowronski family in 1908 whose two lanes, with hand-set pins, are described as the oldest sanctioned bowling alley in the United States.
open_evidence: https://www.geneandmarcyhollerhouse.com/ - official site (seen Sep 2026) takes bowling reservations ($75 first hour) and cites a Discover Wisconsin segment aired Dec 8, 2025 naming it one of Milwaukee's top holiday bars, plus January 2025 visits by Charlie Berens and Lindsey Stirling's group.
notes: Founded Sept 13, 1908 by 'Iron Mike' Skowronski as Skowronski's (Wikipedia); official site says the 3rd-5th generations of the Skowronski family run it 'since 1908'. Marcy Skowronski ran it until her death in December 2019. 'Oldest sanctioned bowling alley in the US' is from Wikipedia and the bar's own site ('oldest certified'); the year the lanes were installed/sanctioned was not verified (Urban Milwaukee's Falcon Bowl article says Falcon Bowl's lanes were sanctioned in 1913, which fits Holler House being older but is not a direct check). Hosted a PBA 'USA vs. The World' event on April 9, 2023 (official site). Hours vary; bowling by reservation only; summer hours limited. The Discover Wisconsin honor is sourced only from the bar's own site. Official site also claims Esquire named it a top 10 bar in America 4 years running (years not given; not listed). No food menu; food relevance low. Not on the National Register per sources checked (Wikipedia does not mention a listing). The business's own site says Discover Wisconsin featured it as a top holiday bar in Milwaukee (2025); only self-reported, so not listed as an honor.

name: Club Garibaldi
iconic_reason: Bay View corner bar and music hall in a 1907 Schlitz tied house, owned since 1943 by the Italian American Mutual Aid Society Giuseppe Garibaldi and known for chicken wings.
open_evidence: https://urbanmilwaukee.com/2026/09/10/weekend-preview-a-milwaukee-renaissance-fair/ - Urban Milwaukee (Sep 10, 2026) previews Strummerfest MKE hosted at Club Garibaldi; official site (seen Sep 2026) lists bar hours daily until 2am and kitchen hours.
notes: Official site: 'Founded in 1907 and later bought by The Italian-American Mutual Aid Society Giuseppe Garibaldi'. Urban Milwaukee (2015): built 1907 by Joseph Schlitz Brewing Co. as a tied-house tavern, dance hall added 1927, society acquired the building in 1943 and still holds title; Joe Dean was sole proprietor of the bar from about 2003 (current operator as of 2026 not verified). 1907 is the building/tavern start; the 'Club Garibaldi' name dates from the society era (exact year not verified). Food: wings and pub fare (about 25% of business in 2015); official site says Milwaukee Magazine voted it 'Best Wings' (year not given, not listed as an honor). No fish fry found. Also a live-music venue. Chosen for item 9 instead of Kochanski's (see drop list). Its presence in an 'oldest bars in Milwaukee' roundup was not directly verified.

name: Landmark 1850 Inn

open_evidence: https://urbanmilwaukee.com/2026/06/30/strip-club-near-airport-closes/ - Urban Milwaukee (Jun 30, 2026) describes Landmark 1850 Inn, 'recognized as Milwaukee's oldest tavern', as the neighbor of the closed Airport Lounge and says it reopened under new ownership in 2024; official site (seen Sep 2026, copyright 1850-2026) advertises a 175-year tradition and a pizza menu.

Closed 2022-2024; reopened March 2024 (drinks first, food later) under a partnership of Joseph Halser IV and former employee Linda Garcia (Dec 2023 plan). The Dec 2023 article said burgers and fish fry would continue; the current official homepage shows pizza, and a current fish fry was not verified (not tagged). Urban Milwaukee also notes Puddler's Hall (1873) and The Uptowner (1884) have stronger 'continuously operating' claims. NRHP listing year 1987 from the nomination date cited by Urban Milwaukee/Wikipedia (listing date itself not checked on the NPS database).

name: O&H Danish Bakery
iconic_reason: Olesen family-owned Danish bakery in Racine since 1949, known for multi-day handmade kringle sold at five area stores and nationally.
open_evidence: https://onmilwaukee.com/articles/OH-danish-bakery-fall-kringles-2026 - OnMilwaukee article on O&H's fall 2026 limited kringle flavors for September-October (Sept 2026, seen in search results; page itself returned 403); official site ohdanishbakery.com footer (c) 2026 lists Durand Ave store hours; Yelp listing for 4917 Douglas Ave 'Updated September 2026'.
notes: Founded May 1949 by Danish immigrant Christian Olesen with a partner (Wikipedia; company blog).
